name: San Francisco
tagline: The oyster bar Anthony Bourdain called a landmark, and three Michelin stars of culinary poetry.

Swan Oyster Depot.description: An 18-stool oyster bar since 1912, described by Anthony Bourdain as a landmark on his travels around the world.

Atelier Crenn.description: Culinary poetry from chef Dominique Crenn in the Marina. Three Michelin stars, and praised by San Francisco Chronicle critic Michael Bauer in his Top 100 list.

Tadich Grill.description: Cioppino and sand dabs with sourdough bread, one of California's oldest continuously operating restaurants.

Benu.description: High-precision Franco-Chinese fusion, the first San Francisco restaurant to earn three Michelin stars, since 2014.

House of Prime Rib.description: A San Francisco institution since 1950, with prime rib carved tableside from a cart and the house salad, just like on day one.

Quince.description: Chef Michael Tusk's French-Californian fine dining in historic Jackson Square; earned its third Michelin star in 2017 and won the James Beard Award for Best Chef Pacific in 2011.

Saison.description: Chef Joshua Skenes's hyper-seasonal, wood-fire cooking in SoMa, one of the most expensive dining experiences in the US; once held three Michelin stars and retains two in the 2025 guide.

Lazy Bear.description: A multi-course communal dinner-party experience in the Mission, born in 2009 as an underground supper club in chef David Barzelay's apartment; now holds two Michelin stars.

Acquerello.description: Classic Italian elegance in Nob Hill since 1989 from chef Suzette Gresham, with one of the city's most celebrated Piedmont wine lists; two Michelin stars.

Californios.description: Chef Val Cantú's fine-dining Mexican tasting menu in SoMa, the first and only Mexican restaurant in the world to earn two Michelin stars.

Birdsong.description: Chef Christopher Bleidorn's wood-fire cooking inspired by the Pacific Northwest, holding two Michelin stars in San Francisco's Theater District.

Angler SF.description: Open-fire grilled seafood and meats from chef Josh Skenes (of Saison), overlooking the Embarcadero; one Michelin star.

State Bird Provisions.description: California small plates served dim-sum style off rolling carts; won the James Beard Award for Best New Restaurant in America in 2013 and has held a Michelin star since 2014.

Rich Table.description: Seasonal Californian cooking in Hayes Valley, famous for its porcini doughnut; held a Michelin star from 2014 to 2021 and now appears on the Bib Gourmand list.

Nopalito.description: Rustic, sustainable Mexican cooking in NoPa, sister restaurant to the Cal-cuisine classic Nopa; no reservations, and a Michelin Bib Gourmand pick.

Cotogna.description: Chef Michael Tusk's casual trattoria next to his Quince in Jackson Square, with pastas and wood-fired dishes recognized with a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Burma Superstar.description: A Richmond District Burmese food landmark famous for its fermented tea leaf salad; expect a wait, since small parties can't reserve.

Mandalay.description: San Francisco's oldest continuously operating Burmese restaurant, open since 1984; named a James Beard Foundation America's Classic in 2024.

Tommy's Joynt.description: A San Francisco hofbrau and saloon since 1947, known for its turkey leg and beer-braised buffalo stew served cafeteria-style.

Zuni Cafe.description: Open since 1979 and famous for its wood-oven roast chicken for two; chef Judy Rodgers won the James Beard Award for Outstanding Chef in the country in 2004.

Foreign Cinema.description: A Mission District restaurant since 1999 with a large courtyard that screens classic films at dusk, from chefs Gayle Pirie and John Clark.

Vesuvio Cafe.description: A bohemian North Beach bar founded in 1948 by Henri Lenoir across from City Lights Bookstore; a gathering spot for Jack Kerouac, Allen Ginsberg, and other Beat Generation writers.

Tosca Cafe.description: A historic North Beach bar opened in 1919 by Italian WWI veterans, famous for its brandy-spiked house cappuccino; restored in 2013 by April Bloomfield and Ken Friedman.

Molinari Delicatessen.description: San Francisco's oldest Italian delicatessen, founded in 1896 by P.G. Molinari; makes its own salami and builds sandwiches on Dutch crunch bread.

Liguria Bakery.description: A family-run North Beach bakery baking Ligurian focaccia since 1911 in the same brick oven used by earlier generations; closes as soon as the day's batch sells out.

Boudin Bakery.description: Founded in 1849 by Isidore Boudin, it's San Francisco's oldest continuously operating business; its sourdough is still made with mother dough dating back to the Gold Rush.

Caffe Trieste.description: Open since 1956 and considered the first espresso coffeehouse on the West Coast; a historic Beat Generation gathering spot in North Beach.

R&G Lounge.description: A Chinatown Cantonese restaurant famous for its salt-and-pepper Dungeness crab, a dish Anthony Bourdain sampled on his San Francisco food travels.

Great Eastern Restaurant.description: A Chinatown Cantonese restaurant known for dim sum and live seafood, which gained fame after President Barack Obama made a surprise takeout stop there in 2012.

La Taqueria.description: A Mission taqueria famous for its rice-free burritos wrapped in a griddle-toasted tortilla; won the James Beard Foundation's America's Classics award in 2017.

El Farolito.description: A late-night Mission taqueria, open into the early morning, and a perennial rival to its neighbor La Taqueria for the title of San Francisco's best burrito.

Taqueria Cancun.description: A Mission taqueria open 24 hours on weekends, beloved for its carne asada 'super' burrito and green salsa.

Yank Sing.description: A family-run dim sum house since 1958, now in the Financial District's Rincon Center, with hand-made dumpling carts and char siu bao.

Tartine Bakery.description: A Mission bakery opened in 2002 by Chad Robertson and Elisabeth Prueitt, whose sourdough and morning buns earned the James Beard Award for Outstanding Pastry Chef in 2008.

B. Patisserie.description: A Pacific Heights French pastry shop from chef Belinda Leong, credited with popularizing the kouign-amann in San Francisco.

Ferry Building Marketplace.description: A food hall inside the 1898 ferry terminal, restored in 2003, home to dozens of artisan food vendors and the Ferry Plaza farmers market.

Bi-Rite Market.description: A Mission grocery store with family roots dating to 1940, known for its curated selection of local goods and its adjoining ice creamery.

Tony's Pizza Napoletana.description: A North Beach pizzeria from chef Tony Gemignani, a 13-time world pizza champion and four-time Guinness World Record holder; named one of the world's best pizzerias by 50 Top Pizza.

Trick Dog.description: A Mission cocktail bar since 2013, known for its rotating themed menus; named to the World's 50 Best Bars list and a three-time James Beard Award finalist for Outstanding Bar Program.

Comstock Saloon.description: A restored 1907 saloon space on the edge of North Beach and Jackson Square, serving pre-Prohibition-era cocktails with live music.
